title: Continuity of the integrated density derivative
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le 1$ for every $z$, and let $v>0$. The function of $c\in\mathbb R^I$ obtained by integrating $f(z)$ times the product Gaussian density derivative at mean $c$ and input $z$ with respect to Lebesgue measure is continuous as a map into the continuous linear functionals on $\mathbb R^I$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Let $A_v(c,z)$ be the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$. Let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f|\le1$. If $v>0$, the linear-functional-valued function $c\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R^I}f(z)A_v(c,z)\,dz$ is continuous.
